solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Small part detached, dropping very loudly (5)

indicators.note: the letters for 'very loudly' are let fall from the phrase

blocks.note: ff = fortissimo, the musical mark for very loud; removed

annotation.surface: A small piece has broken off something, perhaps with a loud crack.
annotation.walkthrough: The break falls inside the phrase: CAME OFF loses its FF, not a whole word.
annotation.definitionFit: A cameo is a small part played by a well-known actor.

entries.clue: Random throw of the dice upset minister (10)

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset turns ROLL upside down, so it reads upwards

blocks.note: chance = random, as in a chance meeting
a roll of the dice; turned over to give LLOR

annotation.surface: A minister so annoyed by a bad throw at dice that he loses his temper.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Upset minister' reads as one phrase; in fact 'upset' finishes the wordplay and 'minister' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The Chancellor (of the Exchequer) is the UK's finance minister.

entries.clue: Minute dash is added into pigment for tanner (7)

annotation.surface: A painter adding a quick dash of colour to a pigment for a leather tanner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tanner' looks like a leather worker; here it is anyone whose skin goes brown in the sun.
annotation.definitionFit: Melanin is the skin pigment that darkens when you tan.

entries.clue: Anybody taking drugs at rave? (3)

blocks.note: E = ecstasy, the drug of the rave scene

annotation.surface: A question whether anybody at all takes drugs at a rave.
annotation.walkthrough: The drug is named by the setting: at a rave, the drug is E.
annotation.definitionFit: One means anybody, as in 'one should always vote'.

entries.clue: Half said dumpy children invented hairy giant (9)

indicators.note: only half of 'said' is used

annotation.surface: Someone reporting that a few stocky children made up a story about a hairy giant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Invented' looks like the children's action; it belongs to the definition, since the sasquatch is a creature of legend.
annotation.definitionFit: The sasquatch, or Bigfoot, is a legendary hairy giant of North American forests.

entries.clue: Put down boiling pot where icy rings persist (6)

blocks.note: sat = put down, placed (as in sat the baby on the chair)
an urn is a large pot for boiling water

annotation.surface: Setting down a boiling pot in a freezing place, where ice rings stay put.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface pits boiling against icy; the rings are Saturn's, made of ice.
annotation.definitionFit: Saturn is the planet circled by rings of ice and rock.

entries.clue: Series of voyages found wrecks in prime locations (4,4)

indicators.note: take the letters at prime-numbered positions: 2nd, 3rd and 5th

blocks.note: start = found, as in found a company

annotation.surface: A fleet of voyages that found shipwrecks at good sites.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Prime' here is mathematical: positions 2, 3 and 5 are prime numbers, a rare but fair device.
annotation.definitionFit: A TV series is a run of episodes, and the starship Enterprise's missions through space are its voyages.

entries.clue: Shaded plants Thrower treated with dung (11)

indicators.note: the letters are processed, worked over into a new form

annotation.surface: A gardener named Thrower feeding his shady plants with manure.
annotation.walkthrough: Thrower reads as a gardener's name (Percy Thrower was a famous British TV gardener), which hides that it is simply letters to rearrange.
annotation.definitionFit: Undergrowth is the low plants growing in the shade of trees.

entries.clue: Traditional brewer still brought over bottles for each boy (3,4)

indicators.note: YET is turned round, in a down clue brought up from the bottom
the outer word holds the others inside it, as a bottle holds liquid

blocks.note: yet = still; turned round to TEY
a = for each, as in £5 a head

annotation.surface: A brewery's old-fashioned still being shipped over, bottling beer for each boy.
annotation.walkthrough: Brewer and still point to beer and distilling; the brewing is of tea. A tea lady brought tea round the office, a fixture of British workplaces.
annotation.definitionFit: A tea lady was the woman who made and served tea in offices and factories.

entries.clue: List contents of shed then sell (4)

indicators.note: take what is inside each word, dropping its outer letters

annotation.surface: An inventory of what is in the shed, before selling it all off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like an inventory; it is the verb for a ship leaning over.
annotation.definitionFit: A ship that heels lists, leaning to one side.

entries.clue: Fifty soldiers occupying small island, threat to constitution? (7)

indicators.note: the soldiers move into the island, sitting inside it

blocks.note: an ait is a small river island

annotation.surface: Fifty troops taking over a tiny island, a menace to its constitution.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Constitution' suggests a political charter; it means the body's health.
annotation.definitionFit: An ailment is an illness, a threat to one's physical constitution.

entries.clue: Electronic component shortened range that gun penetrates (3,4)

indicators.note: the last letter of ANDES is cut off
the gun goes into the shortened range

blocks.note: the Andes mountain range, shortened by its S

annotation.surface: A component whose range is cut short where a gun fires through it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Range' reads as a gun's range; it is a mountain range, the Andes.
annotation.definitionFit: An AND gate is a logic circuit whose output is on only when all inputs are.

entries.clue: Intriguing representation of Acropolis in art (14)

indicators.note: the letters are rendered in a new form

annotation.surface: A fascinating painting of the Acropolis.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Intriguing' reads as fascinating; it means plotting, engaged in intrigue.
annotation.definitionFit: Intriguing, in the sense of scheming, means conspiratorial.

entries.clue: Much-loved animal with book, into trespass somewhat? (5,6)

definitions.text: Much-loved animal with book, into trespass somewhat?

indicators.note: 'into' means entering, so B enters A BIT and sits inside it

blocks.note: a pet is a much-loved animal
to err = to trespass, to sin

annotation.surface: A beloved animal character with its own book, who gets into a bit of trespassing.
annotation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue describes the answer: a much-loved animal with his own book, who trespassed into Mr McGregor's garden.
annotation.definitionFit: Peter Rabbit is Beatrix Potter's much-loved rabbit, star of his own book.

entries.clue: Hot Aga nearly everybody attending stands round (3,3,4)

indicators.note: the last letter of AGA is dropped
ALL THERE stands around AG, enclosing it

annotation.surface: Everyone gathered round a hot Aga stove.
annotation.walkthrough: An Aga is a big cast-iron cooking range found in British country kitchens; 'Hot' seems to describe it but is the definition, meaning fashionable.
annotation.definitionFit: Hot, meaning very fashionable, is all the rage.

entries.clue: Plenty without power welcoming current mildness (6)

indicators.note: 'without' means lacking, so the word must go on lacking its P
'welcoming' means taking a guest in, so LENTY takes I inside it

annotation.surface: Plenty of calm, even without power, when a gentle current comes in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like a flow of water or time; in crosswords it is usually I, the physics symbol.
annotation.definitionFit: Lenity is mercy or leniency, a mildness of treatment.

entries.clue: Settlement agreement banks scrap (8)

indicators.note: DEAL lies either side of FRAY, like banks either side of a river

annotation.surface: A legal settlement in which the banks scrap an agreement.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Banks' looks like lenders and 'scrap' like cancel; the first is a container verb and the second a fight.
annotation.definitionFit: To defray is to pay a cost, so defrayal is settlement in its sense of paying a bill.

entries.clue: Stone mistakenly topped with iron (8)

indicators.note: WRONGLY has its top, its first letter, cut off

blocks.note: st = stone, the British unit of weight

annotation.surface: A stone that was wrongly capped with a piece of iron.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Topped with' reads as one phrase; 'topped' belongs to the wordplay and 'with iron' is the definition, as in ruling with an iron hand.
annotation.definitionFit: To act with iron is to act strongly and firmly.

entries.clue: Due to bra bust not easily moved (8)

indicators.note: the letters are broken apart and rebuilt

annotation.surface: A bosom held so firmly by a bra that it hardly moves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bust' pretends to be the anatomy that a bra holds; it means broken.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an obdurate person is stubborn, unmoved by argument or pity.

entries.clue: Awful place to get RSI, said writer daily (7)

indicators.note: the phrase is spoken, and its sound is spelt differently

blocks.note: dire = awful, and the wrist is where RSI strikes

annotation.surface: A daily writer complaining that repetitive strain injury in the wrist is terrible.
annotation.walkthrough: RSI is repetitive strain injury, which a writer might well get; 'place to get' it is the wrist.
annotation.definitionFit: A diarist writes daily entries in a diary.

entries.clue: Like binary code, cheap in LA (3-3)

blocks.note: a code made of two binary digits, or bits
'in LA' flags American slang for small-time, from an old word for a quarter dollar

annotation.surface: Binary code sold cheaply in Los Angeles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In LA' flags an Americanism: two bits was a quarter dollar, hence two-bit for small-time.
annotation.definitionFit: Two-bit describes both a two-digit binary number and something cheap.

entries.clue: British usurer that goes round making cuts (7)

blocks.note: a usurer lends money at interest

annotation.surface: A British moneylender who goes about slashing budgets.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Making cuts' suggests budget cuts by the moneylender; the blades of a blender spin round and chop.
annotation.definitionFit: A blender's blades spin round, cutting food.

entries.clue: Hunter recalled room full of sleeping children at home (6)

indicators.note: called back, so the letters run backwards, reading upward in a down clue

blocks.note: a dorm (dormitory) is a room of beds, as at boarding school

annotation.surface: A hunter remembering a room full of sleeping children back at home.
annotation.walkthrough: Nimrod is the 'mighty hunter' of Genesis.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the biblical Nimrod was a mighty hunter, and his name now stands for any keen hunter.

entries.clue: Computer came up with specialised Eastern stuffing that family eats? (8,6)

indicators.note: NICHE and E are stuffed inside AROSE

blocks.note: a Mac is an Apple computer
niche = specialised, as in a niche market

annotation.surface: A computer producing a specialised Eastern stuffing for the family table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing' looks like food, and is the container instruction; the definition is a cryptic hint at a family dinner.
annotation.definitionFit: Macaroni cheese is a homely dish that families eat.

entries.clue: 1000 live round boxes? (4)

indicators.note: AMO boxes M, holding it inside

annotation.surface: A thousand live rounds packed in boxes.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: ammunition is live rounds, shipped in boxes by the thousand.
annotation.definitionFit: Ammo is ammunition, live rounds that come in boxes.

entries.clue: Chap heard something of particular interest, delivering kit (7)

indicators.note: the word for chap is spoken, and its sound spelt another way

blocks.note: one's bag = one's thing, as in 'not my bag'

annotation.surface: A man overhearing something that caught his interest, as he hands over a kit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Delivering kit' suggests handing something over; it is the kit a postman uses for delivering.
annotation.definitionFit: A mailbag is the equipment a postman carries when delivering.

entries.clue: Mining area on hard ground loaded with diamonds (7)

indicators.note: the letters are ground up and reformed
the anagram takes D on board

annotation.surface: A mine where the hard ground is rich in diamonds.
annotation.walkthrough: The Rhondda is a valley in South Wales, once a great coal-mining area; 'ground' looks like earth but is the anagram signal.
annotation.definitionFit: The Rhondda valley was famous for its coal mines.

entries.clue: Section of roof tiled again and again (3)

indicators.note: the answer is a slice cut from the words that follow

blocks.note: the last two letters of 'roof' and the first of 'tiled'

annotation.surface: A section of roof that has been tiled over and over.
annotation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the gap between 'roof' and 'tiled'.
annotation.definitionFit: Oft is an old word for often, again and again.

entries.clue: Lasted longer than external broadcast lacking animation? (9)

indicators.note: put on air, so spoken: the word is heard, not seen

annotation.surface: A dull TV broadcast that went on too long.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' and 'lacking animation' look like a comment on a dull TV show; broadcast is the sound signal.
annotation.definitionFit: To outstay is to stay longer than something else, to outlast it.

entries.clue: Clue one answers today? (5)

blocks.note: reads as a solver answering a clue; in fact it names the clue whose answer is ONE
that is, in this very puzzle

annotation.surface: A question about which clue a solver answers today.
annotation.walkthrough: In today's puzzle the answer to clue 3 (down) is ONE, so 'clue one answers' is clue THREE.
annotation.definitionFit: Clue three is the clue whose answer is ONE in this puzzle.
